summary: All 23 SRanger requirements are implemented in 9 Java files (base package sranger). The project compiles under Java 17 and a behavioural smoke test of every transition passes. Eight points the requirements do not settle are recorded below: three invented defaults, four design choices or ambiguities, and one model-abstraction note (obstacleThreshold 0.5 is rounded up to 1 in the model's constants interface).

issues.title: Sensor: value of the 'large default' distance when no reading is available
issues.raw: SR-DM5: 'When no reading is available ... distance() returns a large default value so that the obstacle-detection condition is not falsely triggered.' No number is given.
issues.fix_directive: Chose 1000.0 m (2000 times obstacleThreshold), held in a private constant of Sensor and returned until the first valid reading. Change NO_READING_DISTANCE if the platform defines another sentinel.

issues.title: Sensor: a negative or NaN raw reading is treated as 'no reading available'
issues.raw: SR-DM5 / SR-SF1: distance() is non-negative. The requirements do not say how an invalid raw reading is reported.
issues.fix_directive: Sensor.update(metres) stores the value only when metres >= 0.0; otherwise it stores the no-reading default, so distance() is never negative and an invalid reading never triggers obstacleDetected.

issues.title: Actuator: last command before the controller issues any
issues.raw: SR-DM6: the Actuator stores the latest issued command. Its value before the first command is not specified.
issues.fix_directive: Initialised to Move(0.0, 0.0) (stationary). The controller's constructor overwrites it immediately with Moving's entry command.

issues.title: clockResetTime before the first entry into Turning; clock source
issues.raw: SR-Var1: clockResetTime records when the controller most recently entered Turning. It has no meaningful value before the first entry, and the time source is not specified.
issues.fix_directive: clockResetTime starts at 0.0 and is read only in Turning, after Moving -> Turning has set it. Clock.now() returns monotonic seconds (System.nanoTime) since the clock was created.

issues.title: Moving -> Turning: event trigger, guard, or both
issues.raw: SR-Beh2: transition 'when the obstacle event is received'. SR-GP1: obstacleDetected (distance <= obstacleThreshold) 'is used as the guard on the Moving -> Turning transition'.
issues.fix_directive: Implemented as trigger Obstacle AND guard obstacleDetected, which satisfies both requirements and gives SR-DM5's 'not falsely triggered by missing data' its effect. An Obstacle event while distance > obstacleThreshold is ignored (the controller stays in Moving).

issues.title: Turning: priority of endTask, the timed exit and the tick self-loop
issues.raw: SR-Beh5 (autonomous, time since clockResetTime >= turnDuration), SR-Beh6 (endTask) and SR-Beh7 (tick, no action) all leave Turning. The requirements give no priority.
issues.fix_directive: Order: endTask first (a stop override, also first in Moving), then the autonomous timed exit, then tick guarded by !turnDurationElapsed. If tick came before the timed exit, the timed exit could never fire on a tick cycle. The negation keeps the model's branches disjoint.

issues.title: Initial entry action of Moving issued by the constructor
issues.raw: SR-FR1: on entering Moving the controller issues Move(moveVel, 0). SR-Beh1: the controller begins in Moving at power-up.
issues.fix_directive: The constructor issues Move(MOVE_VEL, 0.0) once, so the robot moves forward from power-up. step() has no initialisation branch. The extracted model's transitions come from step(), so this initial command may not appear as an action of the model's initial transition.

issues.title: obstacleThreshold = 0.5 is rounded up to 1 in the model's constants interface
issues.raw: The model's constants interface rounds a fractional constant up to the next integer. OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD (0.5) is the only fractional constant, and the obstacleDetected guard uses it.
issues.fix_directive: In the extracted model the guard reads distance() <= 1 rather than <= 0.5, so verification of that guard is over the rounded value. The Java keeps the exact 0.5. MOVE_VEL, TURN_VEL and TURN_DURATION are integral and unaffected.

next_step: Run the pipeline (compile, coverage, profile check, transformations, FDR4, Dafny, Isabelle, vacuity) and fix the Java from any failing phase's report.
